title: A bad year at Juilliard
summary: Juilliard was his first formal music school; he skipped for the movies and found the classical students hostile to jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Was your entrance at Julliard your first formal music school?
First formal music school? Yeah; right.
You were primarily a composition student as opposed to an instrumentalist or did they make the distinction?
I had a few courses there, but Julliard wasn't a good experience for me either. I went to the movies most of the

time instead of going to school.
I listened to my instructors at the
beginning but didn't feel any rapport, didn't
feel anything from them, so I gave up quickly.
I dodged around.

You didn't get involved in the student activities there, the
student's bands or anything?

Playing duets with
each other and that sort of nonsense?

I didn't find anybody
there that was interested in what I was interested
in. They were serious, classical students.

I remember trying to play some jazz
in one of the practice rooms and a whole bunch of
them--who the hell is that, who's that? What are
you doing, what are you playing? Like I was
committing a sacrilege, playing jazz in Julliard.
It was a bad experience.
A year. In that year, maybe two weeks. Maybe longer, but I wasn't a good student there.
